about: Foods from data/research/, verified by scripts/check-research.mjs: numbers re-read from the source.

foods.name: Paneer Kathi Roll

units.label: 1 kathi roll
units.basis: INDB serving size (derived: per-serving kcal / per-100g kcal x 100)

foods.notes: INDB recipe uses a maida + atta wrap brushed with half a beaten egg, so diet is 'egg'. Street versions often use more oil and sauces.
foods.image_prompt: Paneer kathi roll wrapped in paper, flaky paratha with paneer tikka, onion rings and green chutney

foods.name: Dates Chutney (Khajoor Chutney)
foods.notes: The sweet chutney used on chaat. INDB recipe has no added sugar (dates only); street versions often add jaggery or sugar. INDB serving ('small bowl', ~264 g) is the recipe yield, so tbsp/tsp are used instead (estimated weights).
foods.image_prompt: Glossy dark brown dates chutney in a small steel katori with a spoon

foods.name: Garlic Chutney (Poondu)
foods.notes: This is the South Indian wet chutney (garlic, shallots, tamarind, dried red chilli, tempered in oil). It is NOT the dry red lahsun chutney used in vada pav and dabeli, which was not found in the allowed sources. INDB serving ('small bowl', ~79 g) is too large for one person; tbsp is estimated.
foods.image_prompt: Deep red South Indian garlic chutney in a small bowl with curry leaves on top

foods.name: Schezwan Chutney
foods.notes: Homemade Indo-Chinese chutney (garlic, ginger, dried chillies, oil, soy, tomato sauce). Bottled brands differ; use their labels when available. INDB serving ('box', 1,553.26 kcal) is the whole jar, so tbsp is estimated. Macro check passes (+5.3%).
foods.image_prompt: Bright red schezwan chutney in a small dip bowl next to momos

foods.name: Egg Roll (Kolkata Style)

source.ref: Egg roll: paratha + fried egg + onion

recipe.cooked_weight_basis: sum of parts; paratha and egg are already-cooked INDB servings, garnish added raw
recipe.method: paratha with a fried egg on one side, topped with raw onion, green chilli and lemon, rolled

foods.notes: Garnish quantities are assumed. Street rolls in Kolkata often use a flakier maida paratha fried in more oil plus sauce, so they run higher. IFCT energy converted as kcal = kJ / 4.184.
foods.image_prompt: Kolkata egg roll in butter paper, paratha with egg layer, onion, green chilli and lemon

foods.name: Kala Chana Chaat

source.ref: Kala chana chaat (boiled black chana, onion, tomato, lemon)

recipe.cooked_weight_basis: assumed: 60 g dry chana taken as 132 g after soaking and boiling (x2.2), plus raw toppings
recipe.method: soaked and boiled black chana tossed with chopped onion, tomato, chilli, coriander, lemon and chaat masala

foods.notes: IFCT has no kabuli (white) chickpea row, so this uses black chana; kabuli chana chaat will be similar but not identical. Boiled yield is an assumption. IFCT energy converted as kcal = kJ / 4.184.
foods.image_prompt: Bowl of kala chana chaat with onion, tomato, green chilli, coriander and a lemon wedge

recipe.method: steamed sweet corn kernels tossed with lemon juice and chaat masala

foods.name: Golgappa Puri (Pani Puri Shell)

source.ref: Golgappa shells: suji + maida dough, deep-fried

recipe.method: stiff suji-maida dough rolled thin, cut into rounds and deep-fried until puffed and crisp

foods.notes: Fried (absorbed-oil model). Street/shop shells, so the 32nd-cycle (reused oil) value is intended; proxy food = Poori (wheat dough) at 180 °C. Dough quantities from a standard suji-maida golgappa recipe (assumed ratio 5:1). Also used as the Raj Kachori shell below.
foods.image_prompt: Pile of crisp puffed golgappa shells in a steel bowl

foods.name: Chaat Papdi

source.ref: Papdi: maida dough with oil, deep-fried

recipe.method: maida dough with oil (moyan) and cumin, rolled, pricked and deep-fried flat

foods.notes: Fried (absorbed-oil model). Street/shop, so the 32nd-cycle value; proxy food = Mathri (maida dough with fat, 160 °C), the closest measured match. Dough quantities from INDB recipe OSR148 (maida 120 g, oil 1.5 tbsp taken as 20.4 g, cumin 1 tsp taken as 2 g).
foods.image_prompt: Flat round crisp papdis stacked on a plate

foods.name: Sev (Besan Sev)

source.ref: Sev: besan dough, extruded and deep-fried

recipe.method: besan dough pressed through a sev maker into hot oil

fat_source.table: Jain, Passi & Selvamurthy 2024: bread pakora, 180 °C, cycle 32

foods.notes: Fried (absorbed-oil model). Shop sev, so the 32nd-cycle value; proxy food = Bread Pakora (besan) at 180 °C per the besan rule. Sev is drier and thinner than a pakora, so real fat may differ. Besan uses IFCT Bengal gram dal (B001) as proxy (besan is ground chana dal). Quantities from INDB recipe OSR147 (besan 184 g, oil 1 tsp).
